body.subject: Codex judge verdict: item48-balances-chain-order-r4 = A
body.text: artifact=item48-balances-chain-order-r4 kind=code purpose=tri7 item 48 round 4 — FINAL bytes: round-3 (A) polish applied (accept-time guard now also verifies the running binary is the new one, and a guard-triggered rollback no longer reports the stale reason), full rehearsal re-run on final bytes; round-4 polish item (empty r1_verdict.json) resolved — the packaged file is populated. Decisions: commit+push to master, and deploy per brief section 7 (DNS3 → Pi → DNS2) worktree=/tmp/codex-judge-skM6iX codex_grade=A judge=codex
reasons: The chain-ordered replay implementation is complete and includes continuity, genesis, hole, fork, known-top, and moving-tip handling, with the legacy file-order path retained explicitly.
Packaged source hashes match 25_source_sha256.txt; Linux tests/builds and Windows cross-build evidence report success, including 937 library tests and all 15 balances-build tests.
The acceptance checker passes all 15 self-tests, including advancing-chain, retry, stale-binary, capped-walk, and snapshot-disagreement cases.

The final deploy harness passes bash syntax checking, verifies the running binary hash at acceptance time, rebuilds the rollback reason after a guard failure, and its final-byte rehearsal covers acceptance, rejection, deadline, failed boot, failed restart command, and rollback readback.
The previously empty-verdict packaging issue is resolved: 22_r1_verdict.json, 23_r2_verdict.json, and 24_r3_verdict.json contain their respective verdict records despite having no trailing newline.
